explain.say: Look at this. Stays the same: your friends, your classroom, school rules, lunch time. Something new: a name, a voice, some new ways. Lots stays the same! Well done. Your challenge: tell a teacher one thing that helps you.

faq.q: Why does a new teacher do things differently?
faq.a: Every teacher has their own style, like their own songs or routines. You will learn their ways, day by day.
asks: Tell me about Some new ways

faq.q: How does the new teacher feel?
faq.a: New teachers can feel nervous too. They are learning your names and your class. A smile helps them.
asks: Tell me about She feels new too

faq.q: How do I tell a new teacher what helps me?
faq.a: You can say, It helps me when I sit near the front, or Can you write the steps down, please? A grown-up you trust can help you tell them.
asks: Tell me about Omar tells her
What do I say to a new teacher?

faq.q: What stays the same with a new teacher?
faq.a: Your friends, your classroom, school rules and lunch time usually stay the same.
asks: Tell me about Stays the same

faq.q: What if I miss my old teacher?
faq.a: That is okay. You can draw them a picture or say hello if you see them. Missing someone shows you liked them.

facts: Teachers often change at the start of a new school year.
A supply teacher is a teacher who covers a class for a short time.

quiz.say: How might the new teacher feel on the first day?
quiz.show: How might the new teacher feel?
quiz.why: New teachers can feel nervous, just like new children.

wrong.1: She is not angry. She is getting to know everyone.

quiz.say: What can you tell a new teacher?
quiz.show: What can you tell a new teacher?
quiz.why: Telling her what helps means she can help you from day one.

wrong.1: Telling her helps her help you.
wrong.2: That would hurt her feelings. Kind words work better.
